question: Pick a group holding a rounded box and the panel says Corner Radius 0 while what you see is round. What should it say?
context: A group has no paint of its own; its corner radius clips what is inside it, and it starts at 0. So the panel is telling the truth and still looks wrong.

options.label: The row says what it clips
options.summary: The number stays 0, because 0 is the truth about the group's own mask, and the row says in a few words that it rounds the group rather than the things inside it. Turn it up and the contents get clipped to that curve, which is what it has always done.
pros: Nothing on screen is a lie
The control keeps doing the one thing it does, and now says so
No row that comes and goes as you move things about
cons: One more line of small text in a panel that already has too many
options.mitigation: It reads as part of the row rather than a paragraph under it, so it costs a label rather than a sentence.

options.label: Take the row away when nothing can show it
options.summary: A group that paints nothing to its own edges has no visible corners, so the Corner Radius row is not offered at all. Put a background on the group and the row comes back.
pros: The panel only offers knobs that would change what you see
Matches how the panel already hides the spacing knobs when nothing can show them
cons: The row appears and disappears as you move the contents around, which is its own kind of confusing
You cannot pre-round a group before you fill it
options.mitigation: The test is on the group's own paint rather than on where its contents happen to sit, so it only changes when you add or remove a background.

options.label: Leave it alone
options.summary: Corner Radius over a group goes on reading 0 with no explanation. It is the honest number for the group's own mask and anyone who turns it up sees immediately what it does.
pros: No new words in the panel
cons: It goes on looking wrong every time somebody picks a rounded group
options.mitigation: Nothing: this is the state today.
